title: Short-Form Video Editor / Clipper
description:
About the work



We're a small US-based company with an established YouTube channel and a growing Instagram presence. Our audience is American, and our content is long-form talking-head and educational video that already gets produced and published on a consistent schedule.



We're keeping our brand name off this post while we hire. Shortlisted candidates get full details on the call.



What we don't do well yet is squeeze everything out of the content we're already making. That's the job.



The role



You'll take our existing long-form videos and turn each one into multiple short-form clips for a dedicated clips channel on YouTube, plus posting to Instagram.



To be clear about what this is and isn't: you're not writing scripts, appearing on camera, or inventing content from scratch. You're finding the strongest 30-60 seconds inside a 20-minute video, cutting it so it holds attention from the first frame, and packaging it so people actually click. The judgment of which moment to pull, and how you title it, matters more to us than transitions and effects.



What you'll be doing

Watching long-form videos and identifying the 3-6 strongest standalone moments in each

Editing vertical clips (9:16) — hook framing, captions, punch-ins, light motion graphics, b-roll where it helps

Writing titles and packaging that earn the click — this is a core part of the role, not an afterthought

Creating or directing thumbnails

Uploading and scheduling to the YouTube clips channel and Instagram (Reels primarily, occasional carousels or statics)

Maintaining a publishing tracker: what went out, when, on which platform

A short weekly report on what performed and what didn't, with your read on why

Requirements

2+ years of paid short-form editing experience. Specifically repurposing long-form into shorts — that's the skill we're hiring for.

A real sense for titles and thumbnails. We care about this as much as the editing. If you can't tell the difference between a title that describes a video and a title that makes someone stop scrolling, this role isn't for you. Click-through rate is the number we're trying to move.

Fluent written and spoken English. You'll be writing titles, captions, and copy for a US audience. Awkward phrasing costs us credibility, so this one is non-negotiable.

Strong command of at least one real editing stack (Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci, CapCut Pro). Tell us which.

Your own computer, reliable internet, and the ability to hit a publishing calendar without being chased. 



REQUIRED IN YOUR SUBMISSION IS A METHOD TO CONTINUE WORKING DURING BLACKOUT. TELL ME YOUR EXACT BATTERY AND WIFI BACKUP YOU HAVE SO OPERATIONS RUN SMOOTHLY. 



Nice to have

Design skills for thumbnails (Photoshop, Figma, Canva at a high level)

Instagram growth experience beyond just posting

Experience with talking-head or personal-brand channels

Familiarity with scheduling tools and performance trackers

Pay, and where this goes



$5/hour, honestly stated. That's the starting rate for a long-term seat, not a one-off project rate.



We're small and we're scaling. The person who does this well — clips that land, calendar always hit, no reminders needed — has a clear path to more: a rate review, then ownership of the clips channel strategy, thumbnails and packaging for the main channel, and eventually managing other editors as we grow. We'd much rather promote someone who already understands our content and audience than hire a stranger into that seat later.



If you want a quick gig, this IS NOT IT. If you want to grow inside one company, read on.



Hiring process

Application (see below)

Short paid test clip using footage we provide

30-minute call

Two-week paid trial, then ongoing

How to apply — please read this part carefully



Applications that don't follow these instructions get deleted without a reply. This isn't a test of obedience; it's the fastest way for us to tell who actually reads.



1. Subject line: Clipper — [Your Name] — [Your favorite short-form creator]



2. Send exactly THREE links to your best clips. Direct links to individual videos — YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Vimeo, Streamable, whatever works. Three. Your best three.



For each one, write one or two sentences: what the source material was, what you did to it, and why you chose that particular moment.



3. Send exactly THREE examples of titles and thumbnails you wrote or made. Screenshots or links are both fine, as long as we can see the title and the thumbnail together. For each one, tell us in one line what your thinking was — and if you know how it performed, say so.



If you didn't write the title or make the thumbnail yourself, don't send it. Send three you actually own.



4. Answer this in three sentences or fewer: you're handed a 25-minute talking-head video with no timestamps. How do you d
 which parts to clip?



5. Tell us: your weekly availability, your timezone, and your editing software.



We reply to every application that follows all five steps.



On the "exactly three" rule: we mean it, both times. Do not send a Google Drive folder, a showreel of everything you've made, a "check out my page" link, or ten examples so we can pick. If you send a folder instead of three links, we will not open it.



Choosing your three best is part of the job. Narrowing down, d
 what represents you, cutting the rest — that's the exact judgment we're paying for. Applications that skip this step, send a folder, or send the wrong number get binned, no matter how good the work is.



Automatic no:



Drive folders or portfolio dumps

More or fewer than three clips, or more or fewer than three title/thumbnail examples

Obviously AI-written cover letters

Work you didn't personally edit, write, or design

A template you pasted into fifty job posts

title: Short-Form Video Content Creator / Editor
description:
Ongoing Freelance Position | Remote | Weddings & Live Events



Marquee Events is looking for a talented short-form video content creator/editor to join our creative team on an ongoing freelance basis.



We are a high-energy wedding entertainment and production company based in the United States. Our weddings combine incredible music, packed dance floors, lighting, production and live entertainment with an energy that often feels more like a nightclub, concert or festival than a traditional wedding reception.



We want someone who can take the footage from those events and turn it into 30–60 second vertical videos that grab attention immediately, tell an epic story and make an engaged couple think:



"I WANT MY WEDDING TO FEEL LIKE THAT."



Content will primarily be created for Instagram Reels, TikTok,
 Reels and YouTube Shorts.



WE NEED A CREATOR, NOT JUST AN EDITOR



We're not looking for someone who simply knows how to operate editing software.



We want someone who can open a folder containing a large amount of raw event footage and see the finished video inside of it.



You need to be able to find the moments that matter, identify incredible 2-second reactions buried inside longer clips, choose the music, create the hook, build the energy and tell the story.



Eventually, we'd like to upload footage from a wedding and be able to say:



"Here's the event. Show us what you can create."



Most of our videos are fast-paced, high-energy and music-driven, but occasionally an event may call for something more emotional or cinematic.



We want to develop a recognizable Marquee Events style while still incorporating new ideas, trends, audio and editing techniques when they fit our brand.



RAW 360° EXPERIENCE IS A MAJOR REQUIREMENT



A significant amount of our footage is captured with an Insta360 X5.



You will receive RAW 360° footage directly from the camera.



We are NOT going to select the camera angles, reframe the footage or export traditional video clips before sending it to you.



You need to be comfortable doing that yourself.



You should be proficient with:



RAW Insta360 footage

360° reframing

Keyframing camera movement

Following subjects

Pans, rotations, zooms and perspective changes

Creating vertical 9:16 shots from 360° footage

Finding unique angles inside a 360° scene

Mixing 360° footage with traditional footage



We don't care whether you use Insta360 Studio, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut or another workflow.



We care about what you create.



If you have never worked directly with RAW 360° footage, this probably isn't the right position for you.



WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING WITH



Our content is primarily captured using:



DJI Osmo Pocket 3

Insta360 X5

iPhone

GoPro/action cameras

Professional cameras

Other miscellaneous event footage



You'll be working with packed dance floors, bride & groom moments, huge crowd reactions, DJs, live musicians, lighting, production, venue shots, behind-the-scenes content, funny moments, emotional moments and everything else that happens throughout a wedding.



Part of your job is taking footage from several different sources and making it feel like one cohesive piece of content.



MUSIC MATTERS



In most cases, you will select the music.



Watch the footage first and choose the audio that fits THAT event.



Most videos will be high-energy, but occasionally the story may call for something more emotional.



We also don't want to hear the same trending audio repeated from video to video.



Strong musical instincts are very important to us.



CREATIVE FREEDOM + COLLABORATION



Sometimes you'll receive almost complete creative freedom.



Other times, we'll go through the footage ourselves and send you a short shot list of moments we absolutely love and would like incorporated.



Think:



"Here are some moments we love. Build something incredible around them."



Even when we give you specific shots, we still want you finding additional moments, selecting the best 360° angles, choosing the music and determining how everything fits together.



We're looking for collaboration, not someone waiting for step-by-step editing instructions.



WE'RE EXPANDING OUR CREATIVE TEAM



We currently work with a content creator who does a good job.



We are NOT replacing him.



We're looking for another creative perspective.



Another set of eyes.



Another style.



Another person who may connect differently with our events and find things in the footage that we didn't see.



Strong RAW 360° creativity is especially important.



THE CONTENT



Our primary videos will be:



Main Highlights



30–60 seconds designed to immediately grab attention and tell the story of the event.



We're also beginning to create:



Quick Hitters



Approximately 8–12 second micro-teasers built around several incredible moments designed purely to STOP THE SCROLL and create excitement for the full video.



Some weddings may also generate additional standalone clips.



During slower periods we may revisit older event footage, and occasionally we'll create larger marketing pieces using multiple weddings, including Year in Rewind style videos showcasing epic moments throughout the year.



WORKLOAD & TURNAROUND



This is an ongoing freelance position, not an exclusive full-time role.



Expect a minimum of approximately:



1 video per week



Many weeks may include 2–3 videos, depending on our event schedule.



There may also be opportunities for additional work through another event professional we work closely with.



Our ideal turnaround for a typical video is approximately:



2–3 days.



Wedding work is seasonal, so volume will vary throughout the year.



HOW TO APPLY

PLEASE READ THIS CAREFULLY.

DO NOT SEND US YOUR ENTIRE PORTFOLIO.



We do NOT want your general portfolio website, Behance page, Google Drive containing everything you've ever edited or 20 different video links.



We don't want to search through your entire career trying to find something relevant.



SEND US TWO LINKS:

LINK #1: INTRODUCTION



Ideally, send us a short video introducing yourself.



Tell us a little about who you are and why you think you'd be a good fit.



If English isn't your strongest language, a written introduction or resume is completely fine.



We'd love to get to know the people who may eventually become part of our creative team.



LINK #2: ONE VIDEO



Send us ONE direct link to ONE video you personally created that MOST CLOSELY resembles the type of content we're describing.



ONE VIDEO. Choose carefully.



It does NOT need to be a wedding.



It could be a music festival, nightclub, concert, DJ performance, high-energy event, sports, travel, lifestyle or anything else that demonstrates the style we're looking for.



Send us the video that makes you think:



"If they like THIS, I'm probably the right creator for them."



If it includes RAW 360° footage that you personally reframed and edited, even better.



ALSO TELL US:

Your experience working with RAW Insta360 / 360° footage

What software you use

Your typical turnaround time

Your price per finished 30–60 second video



And include the phrase:



WEDDING ENTERTAINMENT REIMAGINED



somewhere in your response so we know you actually read this posting.



NEXT STEP: CREATIVE AUDITION



We will review the applications and select a small group of creators whose work most closely matches what we're looking for.



Not everyone who applies will be selected.



Those creators will receive the same folder of RAW footage from one of our previous weddings, including RAW Insta360 X5 content, and will have approximately one week to create a 30–60 second vertical video.



We will intentionally give you creative freedom because we want to see:



What YOU see in our footage.



Your audition video is for evaluation purposes only.



If we love your audition video and would like to publish or commercially use it, we will contact you first and mutually agree upon compensation for that specific video before it is used.



WHAT MATTERS MOST



We're not looking for the cheapest editor.



We're looking for someone who finds the shot we didn't notice.



Someone who looks at raw 360° footage and sees five different possibilities.



Someone who hears a song and immediately imagines an edit.



Someone who can take hundreds of random wedding moments and turn them into 60 seconds that makes someone wish they had been there.



Most importantly:



MAKE OUR FUTURE CLIENTS THINK:

"THAT IS WHAT I WANT MY WEDDING TO FEEL LIKE."



Marquee Events

description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY



Family First Water is a growing, family-focused water quality and whole-home filtration company serving Northern California, & parts of Southern California including Los Angeles, and Inland Empire.



We help homeowners better understand what is in their water through a complimentary, no-obligation in-home water test. Our approach is educational, honest, and customer-focused. We do not believe in aggressive sales tactics or scaring customers into making decisions.



Learn more at 
.

These are primarily warm and previously generated leads, along with some older leads that need to be re-engaged. Your main responsibility will be to speak with homeowners, build trust, answer basic questions, and schedule QUALIFIED appointments for a complimentary in-home water test.



This is not a position for someone who is afraid to make calls or needs constant supervision. We need someone who is dependable, organized, comfortable speaking with Americans, and motivated by measurable results.

* Follow all company scripts, calling procedures, opt-out requests, and customer-service standards.



SECONDARY RESPONSIBILITIES



Once you demonstrate consistent appointment-setting performance, you may also help with:



* Creating and managing
 and SMS follow-up campaigns.

* Building or improving GoHighLevel workflows and automations.

* Using AI tools to improve scripts, follow-ups, call summaries, and marketing content.

* Organizing and cleaning CRM data.

* Assisting with basic social-media posting and content scheduling.



Calling and appointment setting will remain the primary responsibility of this position.



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS



* Excellent spoken and written English.

* A clear, confident, friendly, and easy-to-understand speaking voice.

* Strong customer-service and relationship-building skills.

* Proven experience with outbound calling, warm-lead follow-up, appointment setting, or phone sales.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS



* Experience calling homeowners or American consumers.

* Experience in home services, real estate, solar, insurance, HVAC, plumbing, water treatment, or similar industries.

* Experience creating GoHighLevel workflows,
 campaigns, and SMS automations.

* Familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT.

* Basic social-media or content-scheduling experience.

This is a results-focused position. Performance will be evaluated based on:



* Attendance, punctuality, and consistency.

* Daily calling activity and productive talk time.

* Number of meaningful customer conversations.

* Number of qualified appointments booked.

* Appointment confirmation and show rate.

* Follow-up completion.

* Accuracy and organization inside GoHighLevel.

* Call quality and customer experience.

Review 3-bureau credit reports

Identify inaccurate or incomplete information

Prepare and manage dispute rounds

Review previous disputes before creating the next round

Verify results against updated credit reports

Keep disputes organized and on schedule

Communicate with our Operations Manager

Follow our dispute process and SOPs



VERY IMPORTANT — Our Standards

Files FTC identity-theft reports as a dispute tactic

title: CALLING ALL MASTER - OUTREACHERS
description:
About Us



We help local businesses grow. Part of what we do involves helping our clients open new office locations in new cities, which means every new market comes with a space that has to be found, called, negotiated and secured.



We have already built an AI system that finds the locations. It hands you a list of live options in the target city with the details attached. What it cannot do is pick up the phone.



That is your job.



The Role



You are the caller and the negotiator. Every day you open your list of AI-sourced locations and start dialling.



You confirm the space is real and still available, get the numbers out of the landlord, push for better terms, and build a short list of the strongest options. Those options go to the account manager, who presents them to the client. Once the client picks one, you go back to the landlord and get the deal closed.



This is a phone-heavy role. You will dial, a lot. Some days you will make 40 to 60 calls to find the one landlord who will do a short-term deal at the right number. If cold calling drains you, this is not your role. If you like the hunt and you like winning on price, you will love it.



What You'll Do

Work through a daily list of AI-sourced office locations and call every one

Speak to landlords, property managers, commercial agents and coworking operators to confirm availability, pricing and terms

Negotiate hard on monthly rate, term length, deposit, break clauses and signage rights

Push for month-to-month or short-term agreements wherever possible

Package the best two or three options per market and hand them to the account manager with clear notes on terms and cost

Close the deal on whichever option the client selects

Run the paperwork through to signature and confirm the start date

Coordinate setup: address verification, key handover, signage, mail and utilities where needed

Keep a live tracker of every location, its status, terms, cost and renewal date

Report weekly on calls made, options presented, locations secured and average cost per location

Who This Is For



Must have:



Fluent, natural spoken English with a neutral North American phone presence. You are calling US landlords and property managers all day. They need to be comfortable with you inside the first 10 seconds

Proven phone experience: cold calling, appointment setting, leasing, property management, real estate, B2B sales or collections

You genuinely enjoy negotiating. You do not flinch when someone tells you the price is the price

Organised enough to run 15 to 20 open locations at once without losing track of a single one

Able to work US business hours. Landlords answer the phone 9 to 5 their time, so this one is non-negotiable

Reliable internet, a quiet place to call from, and a decent headset



Nice to have:



Commercial real estate, leasing or property management background

CRM experience

Experience negotiating in a US market specifically

What We Offer

$800 to $1,300 USD per month depending on experience

Performance bonus per location secured, plus a bonus tied to how far under target you land the monthly rate

Direct access to the founder. You will be working with me on this, not through three layers of management

Tools that do the boring part for you. No hunting through listings, no building your own lists. You call, you negotiate, you close

Full-time and long-term. Every client we sign adds locations to your pipeline

A very clean scorecard: locations secured, cost per location, days to close. Hit those and you will do extremely well here

How to Apply



Applications that skip any of these steps will not be reviewed.



1. Start your message with the words MONTH TO MONTH so we know you read this properly.



2. A short intro. Who you are, what phone work you have done, and why this role suits you.



3. A 2 to 3 minute voice recording. Role play this scenario, improvising both sides:



You are calling a property manager about a 250 sq ft office listed at $900 per month on a 12 month lease. Your job is to get them to a month-to-month arrangement at under $700. They will resist. Get the deal.



We are listening for your phone presence, how you handle the pushback, and whether you can hold a friendly tone while still asking for the thing.



4. Answer in writing: what is the toughest negotiation you have ever won, and what did you actually say to turn it?



Shortlisted applicants go to a live call with the founder, then a paid trial task on a real market.

title: Marketing Operations Manager
description:
LEAD THE CREATIVE OPERATION. THEN HELP BUILD WHAT COMES NEXT.

Creative Production is the center of this role at the start. You will manage the editors, own the production system, raise the quality of the work, and make sure strong creative moves from brief to final asset without senior leadership having to manage every detail.



This is not a coordinator role. It is not a virtual-assistant role. We need a Marketing Operations Manager who can operate the day-to-day work and improve the system at the same time.



A NOTE FROM OUR CMO

Before applying, watch this short video from our CMO about the role, its expectations, and what success looks like:





Once Creative Production is stable and you have demonstrated the judgment, leadership, and capacity required, the role will expand into Social Media Operations. That second phase will include the team, publishing, community, creator, affiliate, and channel systems around the content.



Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date. The exact timing will depend on demonstrated readiness and business needs.



ABOUT VERITAS

Veritas builds complete Starlink Mini deployment setups—mounts, power, cables, cases, and accessories—for consumers, work teams, and government fleets.



We are a growing US company with a small, high-output marketing team in the Philippines. Several team members have grown with the company over the long term. We want the same for this role.



THE DETAILS

• Full-time independent contractor role with fixed monthly compensation of $2,000–$2,500 USD, based on experience, leadership depth, and overall fit—not an hourly position

• Approximately 45–50 hours per week, with the regular work schedule fully aligned with Pacific Time

• Philippine graveyard shift: roughly 11:00 PM–8:00 AM or 12:00 AM–9:00 AM, depending on U.S. daylight saving time

• Fully remote and long-term

• This must be your only job. No part-time employment, side hustles, ongoing freelance clients, or subcontracting

• Occasional weekend availability when production, launches, or publishing require management coverage

• Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna required; no regular onsite office days, but occasional in-person meetings may be scheduled



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

At full production, the team aims to produce one long-form video and up to 14 supporting creative assets each week. These may include shorts/reels, static graphics, or carousels and are adapted for distribution across
, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X. 



PHASE 1: LEAD CREATIVE PRODUCTION

• Manage a two-person video-editing team, including their priorities, workload, deadlines, coverage, development, and performance. 

• Turn approved priorities into clear production plans, briefs, scripts, storytelling direction, B-roll needs, and deliverables.

• Own the production pipeline: capacity, assignments, dependencies, revisions, blockers, asset readiness, and delivery visibility.

• Review short-form, long-form, ads, thumbnails, static assets, carousels, platform versions, and other creative output.

• Evaluate the full story—not only whether one shot matches one line. Check hooks, pacing, B-roll, demonstrations, captions, CTAs, factual accuracy, brand alignment, and viewer flow.

• Give editors clear, prioritized, actionable feedback and verify that required revisions were completed correctly.

• Use performance findings to identify stronger hooks, packaging, formats, V2/V3 opportunities, and creative tests.

• Build and improve SOPs, review standards, production trackers, asset repositories, AI-assisted QA, and backup coverage.

• Coordinate minor corrections and urgent production support when needed, without turning the role into a primary editing position.



PHASE 2: ADD SOCIAL MEDIA OPERATIONS

Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date, once Phase 1 is operating reliably and you have demonstrated readiness for the expanded scope. At that point, you will also:

• Manage the current Social Media Moderator and future social media team members. 

• Own the publishing calendar, content inventory, platform schedules, launch pushes, and publishing verification across
, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X.

• Ensure each platform receives the correct version, copy, CTA, description, tags, products, related content, links, and native-platform setup.

• Oversee community, marketing inboxes, important comments and messages, channel presentation, and routine reputation handling.

• Manage routine creator-partnership and affiliate operations, including communication, records, deliverables, logistics, and escalation.

• Own routine UTM, Bitly, campaign-link, profile-link, and destination-verification workflows.

• Review social performance and turn findings into decisions, tests, and coordinated creative recommendations.

• Build and maintain the social department’s processes, AI workflows, reporting, and continuity systems.



HOW THE ROLE FITS

You will report to and work closely with senior marketing leadership. In Phase 1, the video editors report to you. In Phase 2, the Social Media Moderator also reports to you.



You will have authority over routine departmental planning, assignments, quality, coaching, corrections, and process improvements within approved standards. Cross-functional, sensitive, contractual, financial, policy, staffing, reputation, and other material decisions remain with senior leadership.



HOW WE USE AI

Our marketing operation uses AI for context, research, briefs, feedback, quality control, documentation, analysis, automation, and institutional memory.



We want someone who uses AI heavily to improve judgment and execution—not someone who accepts raw output. Sources must be checked. Brand and product accuracy must be protected. What the team learns should improve the next workflow.



YOU'RE A STRONG FIT IF YOU

• Have at least eight years of professional work experience.

• Have at least three years managing teams and direct reports.

• Have at least two years of experience inside a creative or marketing function.

• Have meaningful corporate, in-house, agency, or field-based operating experience—not only freelance, VA, or task-based remote experience.

• Have managed a creative-production pipeline and can explain the team size, volume, process, problems, decisions, and results.

• Are exceptionally strong at storytelling and can diagnose why an edit is technically correct but still wrong for the overall story.

• Hands-on video-editing experience is an advantage, but it is not required. You must be able to direct editors, evaluate their work, and clearly explain what needs to change and why. 

• Can coach editors, address recurring mistakes, manage underperformance, and maintain accountability without becoming the bottleneck.

• Take action without waiting for step-by-step direction and consistently look for ways to improve quality, speed, visibility, and continuity.

• Use performance evidence to improve creative work—not only report numbers.

• Use AI daily with structured context, validation, human review, reusable systems, and feedback loops.

• Communicate clearly in conversational American English.

• Can sustain a Philippine graveyard schedule and occasional weekend coverage.

• Reside in Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna and be willing to attend occasional in-person meetings.

• Have reliable primary internet, a backup connection, and backup power.

• Want one company to grow with for the long term.



THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR

• Someone who waits for detailed instructions before acting.

• Someone whose experience is limited to task-based VA work, short freelance engagements, or managing multiple clients.

• A strong individual contributor who does not want to manage, coach, and hold people accountable.

• Someone who reviews only technical editing details but cannot evaluate the complete story and business goal.

• Someone who creates more process without improving output, visibility, quality, or results.

• Someone planning to keep another job, freelance clients, or subcontract any part of the work.

• Someone testing a graveyard schedule for the first time without a credible plan to sustain it.



HOW WE WORK

Clear priorities. Direct feedback. Strong ownership. Problems are raised early. Decisions are documented. The goal is not to look busy. The goal is to build work that performs and an operation that improves.



Our brand voice follows the same standard: short words, short sentences, confident but never salesy. Like a friend who knows the gear.



HOW TO APPLY

Use this subject line and at least 20 AP:

[INSERT REQUIRED WORD] - [X] years of professional experience - [X] years managing teams



Include the following:

• Your resume with company names, employment dates, role titles, team sizes, and whether each role was corporate, in-house, agency, freelance, or VA work.

• Have you directly managed a creative-production or video-production team? Answer Yes or No. If yes, state the team size.

• Can you provide examples of videos, campaigns, or creative projects you directly led if you advance to the next stage? Answer Yes or No. Do not send links or detailed explanations at this stage.

• In one short logistics block, confirm that this would be your only job and that you would complete all work personally. Include your city or province, most recent U.S.-hours role and actual schedule, primary and backup internet, backup power, and occasional weekend availability.



Note: Applications missing any requirement will not be considered.

title: Marketing & Funnel Specialist
description:
Marketing & Funnel Specialist



About the Role



We’re looking for a hands-on Marketing & Funnel Specialist to join our growing team full time and help build, launch, and improve marketing systems across multiple businesses and projects.



This is not simply a social media or content position. We need someone who understands marketing as a complete system, from the offer and messaging to the funnel, lead generation, conversion, and follow up.



You’ll work closely with David and the team to turn ideas into marketing campaigns, funnels, content, and systems that generate results.



What You’ll Be Doing



• Build, manage, and improve marketing funnels and customer journeys

• Develop marketing strategies for new products, books, memberships, and other offers

• Write and improve copy for landing pages,
s, ads, and other marketing materials

• Create and test offers, messaging, and calls to action

• Support lead generation and customer acquisition campaigns

• Track results and identify opportunities for testing and improvement

• Work with designers, developers, and other team members to launch campaigns

• Use multiple AI models and tools to improve research, strategy, copy, analysis, and marketing efficiency

• Document and improve repeatable marketing systems as the company grows



What We’re Looking For



• Hands-on marketing experience

• Strong understanding of direct response marketing and conversion

• Experience with funnels and customer journeys

• Strong copywriting skills

• Understanding of landing pages, offers, calls to action, and lead generation

• Understanding of CAC, CPL, ROAS, conversion rates, LTV, testing, and tracking

• Ability to analyze marketing problems and figure out practical solutions

• Strong judgment and ability to challenge ideas, test assumptions, and let the market provide the answer

• Organized and able to manage multiple priorities

• Comfortable working independently and figuring out what needs to happen next

• Strong AI skills and experience using multiple AI models and tools together, not simply relying on one AI for everything

• Ability to use AI for customer research, marketing strategy, developing different angles, copywriting, sales letters, funnel strategy, competitive research, analyzing results, and challenging ideas



Our Marketing Philosophy



We believe in direct response marketing, but we’re also playing the long game.



We are not looking for someone whose entire marketing philosophy is:



Sell → Upsell → Upsell → Upsell → Continuity



The first transaction gets someone into our world. From there, we continue providing value, building trust, and making different opportunities available. Customers d
 what they want to buy and when they are ready to buy it.



You still need to know how to sell, but maximizing today’s transaction is not always more important than maximizing the long-term customer relationship.



We’re looking for someone who understands direct response AND delayed gratification in marketing.



What Would Make You Stand Out



Experience with:



• Funnel building and optimization

• Direct response advertising

•
 marketing

• Landing page strategy and copywriting

• Paid advertising

• Marketing automation

• CRM and marketing systems

• E-commerce, digital products, memberships, courses, or books

• Using multiple AI tools/models together for research, strategy, execution, and analysis



This Job Probably Isn’t For You If...



If you need someone to tell you exactly what to do at every step before you can move forward, this probably isn’t the right job.



If changing direction after you’ve already started something frustrates you, you’re probably going to hate working here.



If you become emotionally attached to your marketing ideas and have difficulty letting the market prove you wrong, this probably isn’t the right environment.



If a campaign failing feels like failure rather than information, this isn’t the job.



If you need every project completely defined, organized, and predictable before you’re comfortable starting, you’ll probably be frustrated here.



If being challenged on your reasoning feels personal, this probably isn’t a good fit.



If you’re uncomfortable saying, “I think we’re wrong, and here’s why,” this probably isn’t a good fit either.



If you primarily want to be given tasks and complete them, rather than figure out what needs to happen next, this isn’t that position.



And if your answer to every marketing problem is another upsell, another continuity program, or simply spending more money on ads, we’re probably going to disagree a lot.



On the other hand, if uncertainty makes you curious, failed campaigns make you want to figure out WHY, changing direction doesn’t bother you, and you like solving problems that don’t come with instructions, you may really enjoy this job.



About the Team



You’ll be joining a small, growing team working across multiple businesses and projects. Things move quickly, so we need someone who is comfortable with uncertainty, changing priorities, testing ideas, and taking ownership.



The goal is to help us build a marketing system that can grow with the businesses.



How to Apply



Please answer the screening questions carefully and provide specific examples of your previous marketing work and results.



Strong applicants will be invited to complete a short marketing assignment as part of the selection process.



Screening Questions



1. Tell us about your most recent marketing role and the types of businesses, products, or offers you worked with. What were you personally responsible for?



2. Tell us about a funnel or marketing campaign you personally worked on. What was the offer, what did you do, and what measurable results did it produce?



3. If we gave you a new product with a target audience and an offer, how would you approach creating the marketing strategy and landing page? What would you look at to determine whether the funnel is working?



4. What marketing tools and platforms do you have hands-on experience with? Please include funnels,
 marketing, CRM, automation, advertising, analytics, and AI tools. Also share 2–3 examples of marketing copy you personally created.

title: COLD EMAIL SPECIALIST NEEDED! (PART-TIME,  FLEXIBLE HOURS)
description:
We are looking for a part-time Cold
 Specialist to own our outbound
 channel end to end. Building the lead lists in AI Ark, enriching them for intent signals, writing the copy, loading the campaigns into our sending tool, watching deliverability, and managing the inbox.



We build AI-powered acquisition systems for high-ticket businesses. We work with coaches, consultants, and online DFY service providers.



Clients come to us with one of two problems: they are not getting enough leads, or the leads they do get never turn into paying clients. We build the systems that fix both. Funnels and landing pages, VSLs,
 and SMS sequences, CRM builds and integrations, AI sales systems, and the automation that connects all of it. Our engagements run between $2,000 and $15,000.



The way we win our own clients is cold
. You are not
ing on behalf of a client, you are building the campaigns that bring us new business. You build the lead lists, you filter them down to the people worth
ing, you set up the campaigns, and you work the replies that come back.





PART-TIME. REMOTE. LONG-TERM.



- $75 to $100 per week, plus bonuses based on successful campaigns



- 10 to 15 hours per week, Monday to Friday



- You work your hours inside US Eastern business hours



- Fully remote



That is where we start, not where it stays. Your pay goes up as you progress.





WHAT YOU WILL DO



- Build our lead lists in AI Ark. Pull the companies and contacts, then filter them down to the people actually worth
ing.



- Clean every list before it goes out. Verify domains, strip duplicates, cut the rows that will never convert.



- Enrich the leads and find the intent signals. Are they running ads, hiring, launching something, or posting about a problem we solve. That research is what the copy gets built on.



- Write the cold
 copy. Subject lines, opening lines, follow-ups. We give you the offer and the angle, you write the
s.



- Load the campaigns into our sending tool and get them ready as drafts. You build them, we launch them.



- Watch deliverability. Track bounce and spam rates, flag a domain that is burning, and tell us before a problem turns into a dead inbox.



- Manage the inbox. Sort every reply, respond to the interested ones, and flag the hot ones to us.



- Follow up with leads who went quiet. Most deals close on follow-up 3 through 7.



- Keep the CRM clean. Log conversations, update statuses, nothing falls through.



- Report weekly on lists built,
s sent, replies worked, and calls booked.





WHO THIS IS FOR



- You are genuinely good at list building. Pulling a raw export is easy. Knowing what to cut is the skill.



- You have used a prospecting database before. We run on AI Ark, so knowing it already puts you at the front of the line.



- You will actually dig into a company to find the detail that makes an
 land, instead of sending the same line to everyone.



- You can write a cold
 that gets a reply. Short, specific, and it sounds like a person wrote it.



- You understand deliverability. Domain warmup, sending volume, spam triggers, and why a burning domain has to be caught early.



- Detail work does not bore you into sloppiness. Cleaning a 5,000 row list is a normal Tuesday.



- Excellent written English. Every message you send is the agency talking.





TOOLS WE RUN ON



AI Ark, PlusVibe, Close CRM, Google Sheets, Slack, Notion, Claude, Claude Code. You do not need all of them on day one, but the more of them you already know, the faster you are useful.





WHO THIS IS NOT FOR



Anyone who wants the work handed to them in small pieces. You own the list and you own the campaign, and the quality of both shows up in the numbers every week.





HOW TO APPLY



Do not reply to this post. Applications only go through the form:

title: Sandblast Stencil Production Artist
description:
# Sandblast Stencil Production Artist



Position type: Full-time, remote



---



### The Mission



To deliver 100% cut-ready, error-free vector stencil and engraving files to

our shop-floor operators (sandblast and laser), eliminating machine downtime,

cut errors, stencil failures, and customer-proof discrepancies.



---



### What You'll Own (Your Outcomes)



If you want clear expectations, measurable quality, and room to work without

someone over your shoulder, you will like this role. Success means hitting

six targets:



1. **Plotter perfection (99%+ first-pass cuts).** Prepare vector files with

   zero unclosed paths, zero overlapping lines, and clean node counts so our

   plotters cut right the first time.

2. **Laser engraver reliability (99%+).** Hand off vector/raster files with

   correct hairlines and color-mapping — zero shop-floor downtime or re-runs

   caused by file errors.

3. **Zero sandblast failures.** Verify that 100% of prepped stencils respect

   the physical limits of the medium: minimum line thickness, bridge gaps,

   stable islands, and no clusters of fine detail or dense points that lift

   or tear under blast pressure.

4. **Hawk-eye quality control.** Catch 100% of basic design flaws — typos,

   spelling, shifted elements, misalignments — against the approved customer

   proof before a file reaches the shop floor.

5. **Fast, consistent turnaround.** ⟨v2⟩ 12-to-24-hour turnaround on every

   file-prep request.

6. **Material efficiency.** ⟨v2⟩ Optimize cut-file layouts and nesting to

   cut vinyl, rubber, and material waste by 10–15%.



---



### What You Bring



* **Vector software mastery.** We work in Adobe Illustrator (.ai) and

  Photoshop (.psd). ⟨v2⟩ Fluency in CorelDRAW, FlexiSign, SignLab, or Gerber

  counts if you can deliver clean .ai files.

* **Cut-path and laser preflight skill.** Node simplification, closing open

  paths, raster-to-vector tracing, offset/welding, color-mapping.

* **Firsthand knowledge of sandblast stencil medium.** You have worked with

  sandblast stencil on a vinyl plotter — cut it, weeded it, seen it fail

  under blast — so you know from experience why line thickness, bridge gaps,

  island size, and clusters of fine detail matter, and you fix the file

  before the operator ever sees the problem.

* **Plotter and laser process sense.** Blade offsets, weeding boundaries,

  laser drivers.



---



### How We Work



* On time every day. Keeps commitments without reminders.

* Every problem you see is yours to report — including your own mistakes —

  the same day.

* Check your work against the source. Find the discrepancy before it becomes

  scrap.

* Leave every system better than you found it.

* Raise problems early and directly. Teach what you know.



---



### Why Work With Us



* **Room to do the job.** Clear outcomes, then the freedom to d
 how you

  hit them.

* **The right fit both ways.** We want someone whose strengths match this

  work — precision, ownership, satisfaction from an error-free file.

* **Work that matters.** The files you prepare become the finished memorial.

  Your care d
 whether a family receives a monument that is accurate

  and worthy of the person it represents.



---



### Requirements (all of them)



* Hands-on experience preparing files for sandblast stencil cut on a vinyl

  plotter, and with the stencil medium itself.

* Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop.

* Available during PST business hours ⟨v2: hours to be set⟩.

* A computer and internet connection that handle large vector files

  reliably.

* Before any interview, you fix a vector file we send you that contains

  planted faults, and explain each fix.



---



### How to Apply



Put the words **CUT READY** at the top of your application. Applications

without them are not read.



Send us three things:



1. **Your work history.** For each job in the last ten years: employer,

   dates, your title, what you were hired to do, and the name of the boss

   you reported to. A resume is fine if it has all five for every job.

2. **Your sandblast stencil experience.** Which stencil products

   you have cut, on which plotter, at which employer, in which years. 

3. .Your working hours in PST; your computer specs and internet speed;

   your expected hourly rate in USD.



Do not send a portfolio, a cover letter, or a video. We will ask finalists

for files they are permitted to share.



**What happens next.** We run the same process for every applicant:



1. Everyone who meets the requirements above receives a vector file with

   planted faults of the kind you would catch in this role. You fix it and

   explain each fix. This is a screen, not the decision.

2. If you pass, a 30-minute call. We ask every candidate the same four

   questions: what your career goals are; what you are really good at;

   what you are not good at or not interested in doing; and who your last

   bosses were and how each will rate your performance, 1 to 10, when we

   talk to them.

3. Two to five people go to a longer interview where we walk through every

   job you have held, in order, from the earliest to now.

4. Before any offer, we call your former bosses. You set up the calls.



Please do not apply if your experience is mainly Canva, social-media

graphics, photo editing, or general graphic design without production

vector work. We need someone comfortable preparing technically accurate

files that go straight to production equipment.

title: Short-Form Video Editor (TikTok / Instagram Reels)
description:
We are looking for a talented short-form video editor to help create high-quality Instagram Reels and TikTok videos for Buurteitje, a fast-growing Dutch youth employment brand.



This is NOT a job for basic template editing.



We want someone with strong creative taste who understands modern TikTok/Reels editing: pacing, hooks, sound design, captions, transitions, B-roll, music, storytelling and retention.



You will receive a mix of:



* cinematic footage

* talking-head footage

* UGC creator footage

* drone footage

* app/website screen recordings

* product and behind-the-scenes footage



Your job is to turn this material into polished, engaging short-form videos.



Some videos will be cinematic/vlog-style brand content. Others will be direct recruitment ads aimed at teenagers aged 15–17.



### What we are looking for



* Strong experience editing TikTok, Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts

* Excellent sense of pacing and storytelling

* Good understanding of hooks and viewer retention

* Comfortable with captions, sound effects, music and motion graphics

* Able to make content feel native to social media rather than like a corporate advertisement

* Experience with CapCut, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or After Effects

* Able to take creative direction but also contribute your own ideas



### Important



Please send examples of your BEST short-form work.



We are especially interested in:



* recruitment ads

* UGC ads

* cinematic/vlog edits

* high-retention TikTok/Reels

* modern brand content



Do not send a generic portfolio with dozens of unrelated long-form videos.



### Paid test



Before starting ongoing work, selected applicants will receive the same raw footage and brief for a small paid editing test.



We will compare:



* creative quality

* pacing

* hooks

* sound design

* visual taste

* how well the video feels native to TikTok/Instagram



If the collaboration works well, this can become ongoing work with increasing volume.



Starting rate: approximately $6/hour, with room to increase based on quality and performance.



Expected initial workload: approximately 5–10 hours per week.

title: Short-Form Content & Ad Creative Specialist — Instagram Reels, Carousels & Meta Ads (Full-Time, Remote)
description:
Work directly with a fast-growing U.S.-based healthcare education company in a high-ownership remote role with long-term growth potential, stable USD compensation, and a professional, supportive team culture.



About Us



Zen Psychiatry is an online education and coaching company helping psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners build successful private practices and learn integrative psychiatry through our flagship program, Dream Practice Academy.

We're looking for a full-time content and ad creative specialist to take our organic Instagram output from 5 posts/week to 15-20+ posts/week, and to build out a steady stream of Meta ad creative (roughly 5 new ad pieces/week) — without losing quality on either.



We already have a strong voice, an established audience, and a library of raw material (talks, YouTube appearances, recorded Q&As, past content). What we need is someone who can turn that raw material into scroll-stopping, well-designed organic content and high-converting ad creative, fast and consistently.



This is not a generic VA role. We need someone who genuinely understands what makes content work on Instagram — grid aesthetics, pacing, hook structure, font/spacing choices that don't look like a template default — and what makes a cold-traffic viewer stop scrolling and take action. If you have a personal account (or client work) you're proud of, or ad creative you've made that performed, we want to see both.



What You'll Do:



Organic content (~15-20 pieces/week): 

- Turn raw video/audio/transcripts into multiple content formats: talking-head clips, carousels, quote graphics, repurposed short clips

- Design carousels that are clean, cohesive, and grid-aware — not just text dropped into a template

- Edit talking-head video for pacing, captions, and hooks that stop the scroll

- Maintain visual consistency across the grid/brand over time

- Suggest new formats and content angles as you learn what performs



Ad creative (~5 pieces/week):

- Produce Meta ad variants against briefs and angles we provide (hooks, offers, proof points to test)

- Build multiple creative variations per angle (different hooks, formats, pacing) for testing

- Apply direct-response principles — strong hook in the first 2-3 seconds, clear problem/proof/CTA structure — not just aesthetic polish

- Iterate quickly based on performance feedback once ads are live (we own the strategy and testing decisions; you own fast, high-quality execution)



Across both

- Use AI tools (Opus Clip, Submagic, Canva, CapCut) as a first pass — you refine and polish, not just export raw output

- Work from a template/format library we provide, executing consistently rather than reinventing direction from scratch



Experience required:

- A portfolio is required — organic AND ad creative. Please include a personal Instagram account you run, or organic client work you've done (not a single post — a range of at least 5-10 pieces showing your range across formats) and 2-3 examples of ad creative you've made or admire. 

- Strong eye for design: spacing, typography, color, grid cohesion

- Understanding of direct-response/ad hook structure, separate from organic aesthetic sense

- Comfortable using AI-assisted editing tools, but able to make things look human, not templated

- Self-directed enough to take a raw idea and run with formatting/execution without needing every detail specified

- Reliable, communicative, comfortable with async feedback and iteration

- English fluency for reviewing/writing captions and hooks



Nice to have:

- Experience specifically in coaching, education, wellness, or personal brand content

- Experience with Meta Ads Manager or working alongside a media buyer

- Experience growing your own or a client's account (even small)



Details

Type: Full-time, remote

Pay: $1,200-2,000 USD/month. Pay depends on demonstrated skill level, portfolio, and trial performance across both organic and ad creative.

Start: Paid trial project before hire (details provided to shortlisted applicants)

Hours: Async-friendly; some overlap with US Pacific time preferred but not required



HOW TO APPLY (IMPORTANT)

We use a two-step application process to ensure a strong fit.



Step 1: Complete the application form

Apply here: 



This application includes:

- A short video introduction

- Resume upload

- A few questions about your experience and work style



Step 2: Message us here on OnlineJobs.ph

After submitting the form, send a message with:

Subject: Content Creator Application Submitted – [Your Name]



Message:

 I completed the application form.



Applications that do not complete both steps will not be reviewed.



Thank you and we look forward to hearing from you!

title: Commercial Lease Administrator
description:
Commercial Lease Administrator



Position Summary:



- We are seeking a highly detail-oriented Commercial Lease Administrator to support our commercial property management portfolio.

- The ideal candidate is highly organized, analytical, comfortable interpreting commercial lease language, and experienced working with property and lease data.







Key Responsibilities:

- Commercial Lease Abstraction & Yardi Administration

- Review commercial lease agreements and accurately abstract key financial, operational, and legal information.

- Identify and extract important lease terms, including:

- Base Rent

- Rent Commencement Date

- Lease Term

- Annual Rent Escalations

- Common Area Maintenance (CAM)

- Real Estate Taxes

- Insurance Obligations

- Percentage Rent, if applicable

- Security Deposits

- Tenant Improvement Allowances

- Free Rent Periods

- Renewal, Expansion, and Termination Options

- Operating Expense Obligations

- Other applicable financial or operational obligations

- Accurately enter all lease abstraction data into Yardi.

- Review lease amendments, renewals, assignments, and modifications and update Yardi records as needed.

- Validate all entered data against the executed lease to ensure completeness and accuracy.

- Maintain organized digital lease files and supporting documentation.







New Property Onboarding



When a new commercial property is onboarded:

- Create the property file and applicable property records in Yardi.

- Review all existing lease documentation for the property.

- Create tenant records as needed.

- Enter lease data into Yardi accurately and completely.

- Coordinate with Property Managers to obtain any missing lease or property information.

- Ensure property and lease records are properly organized and ready for ongoing administration.







Tenant Introduction Letters



When a new net tenant moves into a property:

- Review the executed lease and identify the main financial and operational terms.

- Prepare a tenant introduction letter using the company-approved template.

- Include key lease information such as:

- Tenant legal entity

- Property and premises address

- Lease commencement date

- Rent amount

- Rent due date

- Payment instructions

- Other applicable lease obligations

- Property management contact information

- Coordinate with the Property Manager to confirm any additional information before sending.

- Ensure all information in the letter accurately reflects the executed lease.







Lease Commission Invoicing



When a new lease is signed:

- Review the applicable contract or commission agreement for the property or center.

- Identify the commission terms associated with the executed lease.

- Calculate the applicable commission according to the governing agreement.

- Prepare the commission invoice using the company-approved format.

- Confirm all property, tenant, lease, and commission details are accurate before submission.

- Maintain organized supporting documentation for commission calculations and invoices.







General Lease & Property Administration:

- Maintain accurate lease, tenant, and property records.

- Update lease information throughout the lease lifecycle.

- Coordinate with Property Managers regarding lease administration matters.

- Maintain organized commercial real estate documentation.

- Assist with additional lease and property administration tasks as assigned.







Required Qualifications:

- Minimum 2 years of experience in Commercial Real Estate, Lease Administration, Property Management, or a related field.

- Strong ability to read, interpret, and summarize commercial lease agreements.

- Experience working with lease-related financial and operational terms.

- Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

- Strong organizational and time-management abilities.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel.

- Proficiency in Google Workspace.







Preferred Qualifications:

- Experience with commercial lease abstraction.

- Experience using Yardi Voyager or similar property management software.

- Experience creating properties and tenant records in Yardi.

- Familiarity with commercial lease accounting concepts.

- Experience preparing tenant correspondence.

- Experience calculating or preparing lease commission invoices.

- Familiarity with retail shopping centers or commercial property management operations.

title: Social Media & Video Editing for Yoga Teacher
description:
Social Media Assistant (Part-Time, Remote)



Hours: 5–10 hrs/week to start

Pay: $5/hour to start

Schedule: Flexible, but needs regular weekly availability (not sporadic). Content needs to be ready to go before I wake up in the morning (US Pacific time) — the time difference seems to work well for this if you're consistent about hitting that window.



About the Role



I run a yoga and movement business with an engaged, loyal online community — mostly on Instagram (which cross-posts to
). I'm looking for someone to take content creation and community engagement off my plate so I can focus on teaching.



This is NOT a "post and forget" role. My audience is genuinely engaged — posts sometimes take off and generate real conversations and DMs — and I care a lot about responding to people like an actual human, not a bot. That's a core part of this job.



I also really want content that pops — stuff that gets noticed and feels distinct, not generic templated posts. If you have a good eye for what stands out in a crowded feed, that matters a lot to me.



What You'll Do



- Create social media content for Instagram (primary platform, auto cross-posts to
) and TikTok — graphics, captions, reels/short video edits

- Monitor and respond to comments and messages, especially on
, in a warm, human voice (never automated/bot responses — I will not use tools that fake engagement)

- Incorporate feedback and edits efficiently — I'll give direction and corrections, especially early on, and I need someone who takes that well and improves over time rather than needing the same fixes repeated



What Success Looks Like



If this works well, pay can increase to $6+/hour, based on real results after 90 days — increased reach, engagement, and conversion (people signing up for classes/programs because of what you create).



Possible Future Scope (Not Guaranteed Yet)



I'm not committing to this yet, but depending on how things evolve on my end, there's a *possibility* this role could expand to include things like writing newsletters, light video editing (adding music to class videos), video uploading, and some more design work (graphic design, as well as website design on a drag and drop system similar to Wix... but not wix). This would mean another 10 +/- hours per week. I want to be upfront: this may or may not happen, and I don't want anyone applying on the assumption that extra hours are coming. If you're only interested in this role because of that potential future work, this may not be the right fit right now — I need someone who's excited about the core social media scope as it stands today.



Bonus Points If:



- You have experience in yoga, wellness, or movement-based content

- You're familiar with (or genuinely into) doom metal or the alternative/heavy music scene — I teach Goth Ballet and Doom Metal Yoga, and my brand lives in that niche, so someone who gets it instinctively is a huge plus



You Might Be a Good Fit If You:



- Have real experience running social media for a business or personal brand (portfolio/examples requested)

- Write in a natural, warm, conversational voice — not corporate or salesy

- Are comfortable creating simple graphics and short-form video content

- Understand Instagram and TikTok trends and formats

- Can respond to comments/messages like a genuine person, with good judgment about tone

- Take feedback well and apply it consistently (I will be giving edits, especially in the first weeks)

- Are reliable with communication — if something's delayed or you're stuck, you tell me, rather than going quiet



 To Apply, Please Include:

3. Your availability (days/hours per week)

4. Anything else you want me to know

title: Creative Strategist - DTC / E-Commerce (Remote, Freelance)
description:
Growing creative studio producing performance ads for DTC brands on Meta is looking for a creative strategist who can concept, write, and produce ad creative using AI tools. This is not a traditional design role. We care about marketing fundamentals, strong copy, and the ability to turn strategy into finished static ads and video scripts, not your Photoshop skills.

You'll be building ad concepts from the ground up. That means researching the brand and audience, writing the messaging, choosing the format, generating the visuals using AI tools, and delivering final assets ready to upload. We need someone who can think strategically about why an ad will work and then actually build it themselves, not just hand off a brief to someone else.

The brands we work with are DTC and e-commerce. The ads we make are intentionally raw, native, and ugly. Notes app screenshots, tweet style posts, fake text threads, comparison graphics, AI generated visuals, UGC style statics. If it looks like a real person posted it instead of a brand designing it, that's the goal. We also write scripts for UGC video ads and AI voiceover videos, so you need to be comfortable writing for both static and video formats.

AI is central to how we work. We use AI tools to generate visuals, write variations, build statics, and produce content faster than traditional workflows allow. If you're not already using AI tools daily in your creative process, this isn't the right fit. We're looking for someone who's ahead of the curve, not someone who needs to be convinced that AI is useful.

What you'll be doing



Concepting static ad ideas based on brand research, customer data, and performance insights

Writing headlines, ad copy, and full video scripts for DTC brands

Generating finished static ads using AI tools and Canva

Writing UGC video scripts and AI voiceover scripts with hook variations

Working from creative strategy documents and also building your own concepts independently

Producing 15-20+ static creatives and 5-10 video scripts per week across client accounts

Reviewing ad performance data and using it to inform what you create next

Iterating on winning concepts with new angles, formats, and variations



What you need



Experience in DTC or e-commerce advertising, specifically creating ads that ran on Meta or TikTok with real spend

Strong copywriting skills. You understand hooks, awareness stages, pain points, desire language, and how to write for someone who's never heard of the brand

Daily use of AI tools in your creative workflow. Whether that's Midjourney, ChatGPT, Claude, Runway, Flux, Ideogram, or whatever else you use, we need someone who's already deep in AI, not just experimenting

Understanding of direct response fundamentals. You know why an ad works, not just what it looks like. You can look at performance data and make creative decisions based on it

Ability to concept independently. We'll train you on our systems and strategy frameworks, but you need to be able to take a brand's research and come up with original ad concepts on your own

Self driven and communicative. You're active in our workflow daily, responsive, and proactive about flagging ideas or issues



What you don't need



Advanced graphic design skills. We don't use Photoshop or Illustrator. AI tools and Canva handle production

A portfolio of polished brand work. We make ugly ads intentionally. If your portfolio is full of clean corporate design, this probably isn't your lane

Video editing skills. We have a dedicated editor. You write the scripts and concepts, someone else cuts the footage



Bonus



You've worked at or with a DTC ad agency before

You understand Meta's ad delivery system and why creative diversity matters

You've written UGC scripts that were filmed by real creators

You follow the DTC ad space closely and can name 5 brands running great creative right now

You've used AI to build entire ad concepts end to end, not just generate images



Details



Remote, freelance

Monthly retainer with growth as client volume increases

Consistent weekly workload across multiple client accounts

Opportunity to grow into a senior role as the studio scales



To apply

D
 with:



3-5 examples of static ads or video scripts you've created for DTC or e-commerce brands

Which AI tools you use daily and how they fit into your workflow

One sentence on what makes a static ad stop the scroll

Get past the front desk to whoever makes the cleaning decision.
